What do you need help with?

You don’t have to know every office or committee before asking for help. Start with the situation that fits.

Keeping up with the courseMentoring, remedial teaching and accessibility →Settling into college or hostelEveryday campus information →Raising a concernChoose “Complain to us” or contact your college →Finding a form or documentAdmissions and academic downloads →
Student and hostel guide→Committees and welfare→Contact the college office→

Your faculty mentor

Each mentor supports 5–10 students and meets assigned mentees at least once a week. First-year students receive particular support with the transition to medical college and protection from ragging.

Study support and accessibility

Mentors help identify physical, educational and accommodation requirements of students with disabilities and coordinate appropriate support.

Students facing language barriers or difficulty adapting to the course can receive remedial teaching and spoken-English support without bias.

Looking after your wellbeing

Mentors help recognise anxiety, low mood and coping difficulties, and coordinate access to the college psychiatrist or psychologist when needed. Parents or guardians are kept informed of attendance, assessments and wellbeing through appropriate communication.

The Principal holds monthly mentor meetings, with quarterly implementation reporting to KNRUHS.

Tele-MANAS mental health support

Tele-MANAS provides free, confidential mental health support around the clock. Call 14416 or visit Tele-MANAS.

Staying in touch

The MedCampusOS portal lets students and parents follow attendance, assessment reports, hostel outpasses, circulars and feedback in one place.

Contact the college office

If you are unsure whom to approach, the college office can help. Call 08542-227902 or email svsmc_mbnr@yahoo.co.in.
